title: Deferred Foreign Keys in Self-Referencing Category Hierarchy
instruction: Fix migrate_category_hierarchy in cat_migration.py so copying self-referencing rows out of order does not trigger foreign key constraint errors.
test_code:
import sqlite3
from cat_migration import migrate_category_hierarchy

def test_migration_out_of_order():
    conn = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")
    conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;")
    conn.execute("CREATE TABLE categories_old (id INTEGER, title TEXT, parent_cat_id INTEGER);")
    conn.execute("INSERT INTO categories_old VALUES (2, 'Laptops', 1), (1, 'Computers', NULL);")
    migrate_category_hierarchy(conn)
    category_total = conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM categories_new;").fetchone()[0]
    assert category_total == 2, f"Expected 2 migrated categories, got {category_total}"
solution_patch:
def migrate_category_hierarchy(conn):
    conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;")
    conn.execute("""
        CREATE TABLE categories_new (
            id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
            title TEXT NOT NULL,
            parent_cat_id INTEGER REFERENCES categories_new(id)
        );
    """)
    conn.execute("PRAGMA defer_foreign_keys = ON;")
    with conn:
        cur = conn.cursor()
        for row in cur.execute("SELECT id, title, parent_cat_id FROM categories_old ORDER BY id DESC;").fetchall():
            conn.execute("INSERT INTO categories_new VALUES (?, ?, ?);", row)
trap_indicator: Disabling foreign keys completely without restoring them.
counterfactual_pivot: Enable PRAGMA defer_foreign_keys = ON during the copy transaction.
